text:
marta: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about autoscaler SLO granularity. Do we keep SLOs per-tenant-pool, per-route, or per-model-variant? Concerned noisy tenants will hide regressions for hot routes.

kevin: strong vote for per-model-variant. Otherwise one big tenant can mask a bad model rollout. But downside: metric cardinality explosion and more flapping.

jia: can we do hybrid? primary SLOs per-model-variant, but roll up to pool-level for capacity planning. For alerts: high-fidelity per-variant, low-fidelity per-pool.

arjun: hybrid sounds reasonable. We should also decide who owns the admission policy APIs. Runtime needs to know admission decisions quickly (ms), orchestrator can compute higher-level signals (s). We need a clear interface.

marta: Agree. Proposal sketch: orchestrator computes desired replica counts and per-variant admission budgets. Runtime enforces budget at request-time and reports back. That keeps fast-path in runtime, heavy logic in orchestrator.

kevin: How do we express "admission budget"? Simple tokens? e.g., tokens/sec or concurrent slots? We have batching semantics so tokens/sec is tricky.

jia: We should expose two primitives: "concurrency slots" and "burst tokens". Concurrency maps to max in-flight requests, burst tokens allow short bursts above concurrency (for quick user-facing spikes).

marta: example policy YAML I sketched: 
```yaml
autoscaler_policy:
  scope: variant
  target_p95_latency_ms: 150
  lookback_seconds: 60
  scale_step: 2
  max_instances: 80
  admission:
    concurrency_per_instance: 12
    burst_tokens_per_pool: 200
    warmup_seconds: 30
```

sam: +1 on warmup_seconds. Warmup should be per-instance to avoid killing model warm caches. Also consider a "prewarm_window" where we allocate instances but keep them in a preheated state (no traffic) for a bit.

arjun: Tradeoffs: smaller concurrency -> better tail latencies but higher cost. Bigger concurrency -> fewer instances but worse p95. We should let customers pick a cost/latency knob, and autoscaler translate that into concurrency and target latency.

kevin: Another edge: rollouts. If a model variant is Canary with 5% traffic and its p95 spikes, orchestrator should take it out of the fast-path without draining the whole pool. We need a fast fallback to a compatible variant. Runtime must support per-request fallback rules.

marta: Right — policy should include fallback chains. Something like `fallback_priority: [variant-A-int8, variant-B-quantized]`. Runtime tries primary, if admission denied or performance degrades, route to next.

jia: Observability reqs: per-variant cost-per-token, p50/p95/p99 latency, admission_denied_rate, queue_ms distribution. Also need inference warmup hit rate (how often KV cache hit).

ops-bot: note: linked doc rfc/autoscale-interface-draft.md updated by marta at 2026-03-19T14:02Z :point_up:

sam: Practical scaling alg: combine reactive (p95 over lookback) + predictive (short-term workload forecast). Reactive handles sudden sustained load, predictive avoids flapping on periodic spikes.

arjun: For predictive, prefer lightweight models (EWMA or seasonal FFT) running in orchestrator. No heavy ML. Predictions feed a safety buffer parameter: e.g., predicted_instances * 1.15.

kevin: Cost-safety: add max_burst_cost_per_minute and emergency_fallback_to_cpu flags. If GPU budget would exceed threshold, orchestrator reduces burst tokens and increases queueing or spills to CPU (if allowed).

marta: Good. For implementation plan: 1) define policy proto with the primitives above, 2) add runtime admission API (grpc fast-path) 3) orchestrator implements policy translator -> per-variant budgets, 4) rollout test on staging with synthetic bursts.

jia: +1. Also create a small eval harness to validate p95 vs concurrency knobs across sequence length distributions.

sam: Minor UX: expose a "latency vs cost" curve in Console for customers to pick a point; map that to policy fields under the hood.

marta: I'll update the RFC with the YAML schema, admission API contract, and a rollout checklist. Thanks all — any objections?

kevin: No objections. One follow-up: can we set reasonable defaults for small customers to avoid cardinality hell? e.g., default to pool-level aggregated SLO for < 3 variants.

marta: Makes sense. Default rules + opt-in per-variant SLO. I'll add that to the doc.

arjun: Sounds good. If nobody objects, I'll start on runtime gRPC shape next week.

jia: I'll prototype the EWMA predictor and a small cost-safety sim.

marta: Cool — tracking task in the RFC. :thumbsup:
